examples.knowledge_point: Writing First-Order Linear ODEs in Standard Form
examples.problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}
+
y\sin x
-
\cos x
=0
$$
examples.worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}
+
P(x)y
=
Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\sin x$ and $Q(x) = \cos x.$
